answer: Sybil resistance can rest on per-agent history clones cannot copy. Enrollment gives each key a sealed vault with a random seed; each epoch the agent proves work over it, then reseals. Its transcript branches like a willow, one tip per epoch, so a duplicated vault yields identical tips and is caught. Weight needs a spiral of ninety consecutive proofs, each extra key from the same funder starting one turn further out. A thousand-agent farm must fund a thousand parallel histories, and one skipped epoch resets the key. Recurring upkeep, not one deposit, pushes attacker cost above the votes bought.
